iOS 27 brings several new features to Apple Wallet, one of which is an Apple Card exclusive feature—a hub that centrally manages all recurring transactions. I really wish every card had this feature.

iOS 27 consolidates Apple Card recurring transactions for easy tracking of subscription services

In this increasingly digital world, subscription services are becoming more common, so it's easy to forget exactly what you've signed up for.

There are indeed plenty of apps and services on the market that claim to help you track subscriptions, but handing over your financial information to third parties always raises privacy concerns. Fortunately, Apple Card users will soon no longer need such services.

In iOS 27, the Wallet app adds a recurring transactions feature for Apple Card users.

When viewing your Apple Card in iOS 27, a new "Recurring" option appears in the three-dot menu in the top right corner.

Tap it to display a list of upcoming recurring transactions, and you can also use calendar mode to view the entire month at a glance.

I consider myself pretty aware of what I've subscribed to, but even so, it takes effort to keep track. This new Apple Card feature makes tracking subscriptions incredibly easy.

I especially love the calendar view mode, which lets me see at a glance the expected charge date for each payment—it's really convenient.

iOS 27 lists recurring transactions based on your Apple Card transaction history, so it may not detect everything. The Wallet app includes a disclaimer stating: "The dates and amounts shown are predicted based on your transaction history and may not be fully accurate. Everyday purchases may be mistakenly identified as recurring transactions."

If you find an item incorrectly flagged as a recurring transaction, fixing it is simple.

I really hope this Apple Card feature inspires more credit cards and banks to follow suit. This new iOS 27 feature is something every card should have as a basic offering.

Now I really want to switch all my subscriptions to pay with Apple Card.
